method: Use the spherical Web Mercator XYZ tiling scheme at integer zooms 0 through 30. For a WGS84 latitude and longitude, with latitude limited to ±85.0511287798066 degrees and longitude to ±180 degrees, calculate x = floor((longitude + 180) / 360 × 2^zoom) and y = floor((1 − asinh(tan(latitude)) / π) / 2 × 2^zoom), using radians for the trigonometric operations. Clamp the positive 180-degree longitude and exact northern/southern limits to the final valid tile index. Reverse conversion uses longitude = x / 2^zoom × 360 − 180 and latitude = atan(sinh(π × (1 − 2y / 2^zoom))) for the northwest corner, with x + 1 and y + 1 giving the southeast corner and half-index offsets giving the center. The quadkey interleaves Y and X bits from most to least significant, with digit = xBit + 2 × yBit; zoom zero has an empty quadkey. Coordinate strings accept ordinary decimal notation with up to 13 fractional digits and no exponents. Tile indexes must be integers within the selected zoom's grid. Displayed coordinates are rounded to ten decimal places. This performs no datum transformation, routing, geocoding or map request, and nothing is stored or transmitted.
